clue.text: Bishop, religious sort of soul who'd fight crime?

parts.note: B is the chess notation abbreviation for bishop
in Hindu philosophy the atman is the individual soul or self

explanation.surface: A churchman of spiritual bent wonders whether he is the sort to take on criminals.
explanation.definitionFit: The comic-book hero spends his nights battling villains in Gotham, so he is someone who fights crime.

clue.text: One helping a runner to go up in the world?

definitions.text: One helping a runner to go up in the world?

parts.words: One helping a runner to go up in the world?
parts.note: reads like a mentor for an ambitious athlete, but the runner is a climbing bean, trained up a tall stick

explanation.definitionFit: A tall garden stake supports runner beans as they climb, literally helping them rise.

clue.text: Down-and-out uses deception to bring in millions

indicators.note: the trickery word takes the abbreviation inside itself

parts.note: to trap someone is to catch them by trickery
M is the standard abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A destitute person resorts to trickery to rake in vast sums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bring in' puts M inside TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: A vagrant with no home or money is a destitute person, someone utterly down on their luck.

clue.text: Little woman always cuddling male

indicators.note: to cuddle is to wrap one's arms round, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: ay (or aye) is an old and poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A small woman is forever hugging a man.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy March is one of the four sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women.
explanation.definitionFit: The youngest March sister in the novel Little Women is a literary example of a little woman.

clue.text: Not on the right track, one of the females will get lost, naturally

indicators.note: getting lost means disappearing, so a letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: a ship or plane straying from its route is off course
F is the abbreviation for female, and this phrase removes just one such letter

explanation.surface: A woman who strays from the proper path vanishes, as one would expect.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF COURSE has two Fs; dropping one leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both expressions mean as might be expected, certainly; synonyms used as replies or sentence adverbs.

clue.text: Horror about drug in cargo

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for horror goes round the drug

parts.note: horror is fright or terror
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Alarm at narcotics discovered in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried by ship, train or truck are synonymous with cargo.

clue.text: Into the next valley or past it?

definitions.meaning: crossing the ridge takes one down into the valley beyond
an idiom for someone too old to do something well

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means beyond the summit and figuratively means too old, both senses in the clue.

clue.text: Abandoning rut, soar 'up, feeling so?

indicators.note: acting with abandon means wildly and without restraint, so these letters run wild

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Leaving one's routine behind and soaring upwards, how elated must one feel?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' is the anagram signal: the letters of RUT plus SOAR UP rearrange to make the answer. The apostrophe is an OCR mark; the page reads 'soar up'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone escaping a rut and soaring would feel ecstatic, which is a synonym of the adjective.

clue.text: No longer be inclined to make offer?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer what one was
to tend is to be inclined or apt to do something

explanation.surface: A one-time inclination now gone, it seems, before the offer is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a lost inclination; the definition is the verb in 'extend an invitation'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend an invitation or the hand of friendship is to offer it, a synonym sense.

clue.text: Cell with barrier yours truly gets locked in

indicators.note: being locked in means enclosed, so the self-reference sits inside the barrier

parts.note: a gate is a barrier across an opening
the speaker's way of referring to oneself, me

explanation.surface: Someone finds themselves shut in a prison cell behind a gate.
explanation.walkthrough: The prison cell picture misleads; the cell here is biological, a reproductive one.
explanation.definitionFit: A reproductive sex cell, such as a sperm or egg, is a specific biological kind of cell.

clue.text: Whatever may happen, regardless of the cost?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning in any case, anyway
literally at whatever price or rate is charged

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means anyway idiomatically and, read literally, at any price charged.

clue.text: One living abroad wants English Times? Just so!

parts.note: X is the multiplication sign, read as times
pat means exactly right, just so, as in an answer off pat

explanation.surface: An emigrant longs for the London newspaper, and that is exactly right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, italicised on the page, but it is the times sign X.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant settled outside their homeland is commonly called by this short form of expatriate.

clue.text: Sheet anchor

parts.note: a sheet anchor is a ship's spare anchor or a mainstay, but read literally it is something holding sheets of paper down

explanation.definitionFit: A heavy desk ornament keeps loose sheets of paper from blowing away, anchoring them in place.

clue.text: Justification for being in Paris

parts.note: asks why one would visit the French capital, but means the French phrase for the reason a thing exists

explanation.definitionFit: The French expression literally translates as reason for being, a thing's main purpose or justification.

clue.text: It may have burnt contents

indicators.note: the contents of a word are the letters inside it, here the middle of burnt

explanation.surface: A vessel for cremated ashes holds what is left after burning.
explanation.definitionFit: A funerary vase holds cremated ashes, which are literally burnt remains inside it.

clue.text: Coal left to catch fire

parts.note: to ignite is to catch fire or burst into flame

explanation.surface: Fuel abandoned in a heap starts to burn.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown coal, soft and low grade, is a type of coal used as fuel.

clue.text: Not be wanted to roam the streets accosting people

definitions.meaning: an idiom for something on offer that nobody takes up
literally to wander about soliciting passers-by for money

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase idiomatically means to find no takers, and literally to live by soliciting alms.

clue.text: The northern slave gets everything

parts.note: in northern English dialect, the word the is shortened to t', as in Yorkshire speech
a helot was a serf or slave in ancient Sparta

explanation.surface: The slave from the north ends up with the whole lot.
explanation.walkthrough: T' is the Yorkshire and Lancashire form of the definite article.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the entire amount, all of it, an idiomatic equivalent of everything.

clue.text: Violent man agreed to bump off a police officer

indicators.note: violent treatment throws the letters about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A thug consents to murder a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to bump off' removes A from the letters of MAN AGREED; the remaining eight, rearranged after 'Violent', give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: In France a gendarme is a member of the armed police, so a police officer.

clue.text: Cannot abide a black beast with tail cut off

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: cutting off the tail removes the final letter of the word

parts.note: a horse is a large beast

explanation.surface: Someone loathes a dark animal that has had its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with tail cut off' removes E from HORSE, leaving HORS.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe or detest something is to be unable to bear it, a synonym phrase.

clue.text: Sister in convent carrying large piece of embroidery

indicators.note: to carry is to hold, so the abbreviation holds the word for large inside

parts.note: Sr is the abbreviated title for a nun, a sister in a convent
ample means large or generous

explanation.surface: A nun in her convent bears a large needlework piece.
explanation.walkthrough: The convent belongs to the abbreviation, a nun's title, rather than being a container.
explanation.definitionFit: An embroidered cloth showing a range of stitches, alphabets and mottoes is a classic example of needlework.

clue.text: A matter of biological significance under discussion

parts.note: tissue is organic material made of cells, matter of biological significance

explanation.surface: A biologically important question is being debated.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means currently being debated or in dispute, an idiomatic synonym.

clue.text: Utter a right tirade

parts.note: a rant is a tirade, a long angry speech

explanation.surface: Deliver a proper diatribe.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective utter means complete or out-and-out, matching the synonym used of a rogue or fool.

clue.text: Foolish boss, holy within

indicators.note: the word for holy goes within the word for boss

parts.note: a boss is a raised ornament or knob, and so is a stud
pi is slang for pious or holy

explanation.surface: A silly manager hides a sanctimonious streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager, but here it is a raised knob or ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid and foolish are synonymous adjectives meaning lacking good sense.

clue.text: Ticket for game

definitions.meaning: a label or ticket attached to an item, giving price or identity
a children's chasing game in which one player touches another

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an attached label and a playground chasing game, matching both senses.

clue.text: Soldier made out to be despairing

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier is shown to be in despair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of SOLDIER MADE.
explanation.definitionFit: Having lost heart and confidence, someone downcast is despairing.

clue.text: Don't slouch, taking drink to swallow it

indicators.note: swallowing takes something in, so the drink word holds the other piece

parts.note: to sup is to drink, especially in sips
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to straighten one's posture while taking a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is an imperative: the instruction to someone who is slouching.
explanation.definitionFit: The imperative command to sit up straight is the opposite of an order to slouch.

clue.text: Cricketer will want a beer having collected a duck

indicators.note: collecting means gathering in, so the beer holds the zero

parts.note: a pint is a glass of beer
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, so it gives the letter O

explanation.surface: A cricket player fancies a drink after being out without scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Point is a fielding position on the off side in cricket, and so the fielder standing there.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket point is a fielding position, and the fielder there is called by its name.

clue.text: University's high flyer?

definitions.meaning: ... has its own university, so a place known for its university
the Avro ... was a Second World War heavy bomber, a plane flying high

explanation.definitionFit: The name belongs to an English university town and to a famous wartime bomber aircraft.

clue.text: A short distance behind

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for foot or feet, a short distance

explanation.surface: Just a little way to the rear.
explanation.definitionFit: On a ship this word means toward the stern, so behind or at the back.

clue.text: Constable seen as reverse of divine being, by admitting sin

indicators.note: reverse here asks for the word for deity to be read backwards

parts.note: a god is a divine being

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the little word takes the sin inside

parts.note: taken as written
to err is to sin or go astray

explanation.surface: A policeman looks the opposite of godly, next to an admission of wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Dogberry is the bumbling constable in Shakespeare's Much Ado About Nothing; 'Constable' looks like the painter but is the watchman.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comic watchman Dogberry is a literary example of a constable.

clue.text: Chief no longer performing well keeps power

indicators.note: keeping means holding, so the stale word holds the power letter

parts.note: an athlete gone stale has lost form through overtraining
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A leader past their best clings on to power.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means main or principal, as in a staple diet, so chief.
